Marissa — quick answers and a recommend matrix below. Dev, please chime in if any infra/cost numbers need adjusting.

Proposed eval matrix (3 variants):
1) redwood-gpt-13b-long-context (specialized long-context)
   - Window: 128k tokens (native long-context model)
   - Pros: minimal truncation, good summarization fidelity on windows up to 80k
   - Cons: higher GPU memory; slightly higher per-token cost

2) redwood-llama-70b-q4 (latency/quality balance)
   - Window: 32k tokens (with KV cache + prefix stitching)
   - Pros: strong quality, lower latency with batching, mature quantized runtimes
   - Cons: may require progressive summarization for >32k contexts; quantization can slightly affect factuality for sensitive docs

3) redwood-mix-small (cost-optimized routing)
   - Window: 16k tokens
   - Pros: low cost for recall-ish tasks, good for bulk background processing
   - Cons: not ideal for fidelity-critical summaries

Truncation behavior / handling recommendations:
- For interactive UX: use KV caching + prefix-preserving rolling window for session history; for archival multi-doc summarization, run hierarchical summarization (chunk -> intermediate summaries -> final synthesis).
- Provide explicit truncation markers in outputs and include warning flags when content is dropped.

Quality/fidelity measurement suggestions:
- Automated: ROUGE/L Rouge-L, token-level overlap, and a heuristic "hallucination score" (detect hallucinated entities by cross-referencing with provided ground-truth).
- Human: targeted human checks on 10% of high-risk prompts + blind A/B against baseline.
- Regression: snapshot model outputs and run daily evals on the prompt set; alert on >5% drop in fidelity metrics.

Attachments we should send to Acme: prompt_set_v1.csv (sample prompts + expected answers), short eval plan doc, and a stub benchmark PDF. I can generate initial run results on the hosted sandbox and upload to the Drive link Vivek referenced (see links below).
